goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so any booking with an empty/null destinationCalendar array (e.g. `[]` set by many of the updated call sites, or `null` from handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067) and location `integrations:google:meet` throws a TypeError inside `create()`, crashing the whole booking-creation request instead of the old safe optional-chained fallback.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the code now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without guarding for `undefined`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array (`[]`), destructuring yields `undefined` and accessing `.integration` will throw a `TypeError`. The diff also shows multiple call sites now setting `destinationCalendar` to `[]` (e.g. webhook/cron/payment handlers) and `handleNewBooking` can set it to `null`, making this crash scenario real when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (organizer has no personal destinationCalendar and eventType has none set), so collective co-hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped — defeating the stated purpose of this PR (handle collective multiple host destinationCalendar)

adjudication.rationale:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set:
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar
  ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar
  ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar]
  : null,
```
Later, for collective team events, co-host destination calendars are added via optional chaining:
```ts
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```
If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, this push is a no-op, so `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently dropped even when populated. This directly breaks the intended behavior of including collective co-hosts' destination calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — In `create()`, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` now hardcodes `undefined` for non-calendar (video) results, whereas the old code used `result.credentialId` for that branch, potentially losing the video credential reference stored on the booking

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` within `create()`, the mapping that builds booking reference objects changed `credentialId` from `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. This means for non-calendar results (e.g., video/conferencing integrations), any `result.credentialId` that was previously persisted will now be dropped (set to `undefined`), which can lose the credential reference associated with the created meeting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:343 — Credential fallback ("find in memory, else fetch from DB and manually rebuild a Credential-shaped object with appName/id/type/key/userId/teamId/invalid/appId") is copy-pasted verbatim at EventManager.ts:343 (createAllCalendarEvents), EventManager.ts:516 (updateAllCalendarEvents), and reimplemented with subtly different (less complete) logic at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:432 — a bug fix or field addition to one copy (e.g. missing app.slug select) will silently not apply to the others.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same “find credential in this.calendarCredentials, else prisma.credential.findUnique + manually rebuild CredentialWithAppName” pattern duplicated in packages/core/EventManager.ts in both createAllCalendarEvents (new DB fetch + manual object with app.slug include) and updateAllCalendarEvents (similar DB fetch + manual object). A similar fallback is also added in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, but it fetches prisma.credential without including app.slug and does not rebuild the same CredentialWithAppName shape. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture risk introduced by the change: future fixes/field additions can diverge across copies and silently not apply everywhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when the organizer/eventType has no destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null), so collective team members' destinationCalendars are dropped with no error — defeating the exact multi-host fix this PR claims to add

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events it does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Because `evt.destinationCalendar` can be `null`, the optional chaining causes a silent no-op and the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are never added, dropping team members’ destination calendars without error.
